title: To Vitruvian Physique: Don't do it, bro
summary: Response to natural YouTuber Vitruvian Physique (Igor) considering TRT after bloodwork showed low testosterone following a contest prep. NH argues the T-level obsession comes from PED culture, that low T after prep is a symptom of extreme dieting and lifestyle that should be fixed rather than band-aided, and that natural influencers going on TRT blackpill their young audiences.
claims: The modern obsession with testosterone levels among natural lifters was imported from PED users; lifters used to just train without ever thinking about hormones
Getting your T levels tested without a medical reason mostly creates a self-image problem: bad results make you look down on yourself even if you look great
Many young men get bloodwork hoping to find an excuse that explains why they are small and justifies TRT, instead of first training and eating properly
Raising testosterone naturally is simple: clean diet, lots of sleep, low stress and rigorous training sustained for years
Bodybuilding contest prep is horrible for health, even natural: getting extremely lean, dehydrating and depleting nutrients wrecks your hormonal profile
Modern natural bodybuilding is just pro bodybuilding without the hormones, copying stage standards set by drug users
Physique competitors a hundred years ago were 10-16%, sometimes 18% body fat, untanned and unpumped, and still looked tremendous
Naturals should turn their backs on stage-lean competition standards because they are what produces low testosterone
Staying at a healthy body fat would likely have avoided the low-T problem after prep
Young men chasing year-round shredded leanness sabotage both their progress and their health
Differences in testosterone between naturals are small; the meaningful gap is between naturals and enhanced lifters who have 3-4x the hormones
At 30 a man is not at an age where declining hormones are legitimate; most men peak in their 30s-40s and your prime comes after 20 years of training
If your hormones are in the normal range or slightly below, they are almost irrelevant for a natural lifter
TRT is marketed as health from a clinic to remove the stigma of PEDs, but it is often just an excuse
When a respected natural in his 30s contemplates TRT, it tells his young audience that years of natural work were for nothing, pushing teenagers to jump on TRT immediately
Youth/TRT clinics push the candidate age as low as possible for profit; with the right bloodwork and payment almost anyone can get prescribed
Low testosterone is your body signalling you are doing something wrong (e.g. starving it); TRT is a band-aid that does not fix the cause
Most teenagers have low T because of video games, fast food and no training: a lifestyle problem, not a medical one
At 17 he believes his T was far below normal range, but he never tested and fixed his environment instead; he expects it is now mid-to-high range
Influencers with young audiences have a responsibility not to promote TRT
The narrative that TRT is the next step of male evolution because modern T levels are low is transhumanism pushed by people profiting from testing and supplements
Going on TRT after a natural show tanks your testosterone is self-sabotage followed by injection; a natural bodybuilder should be healthy, big and lean all year
A fake natty influencer only takes a syringe and a vial; a genuine natural influencer takes a decade of work, which is why so few exist
Once a natural goes on TRT his advice is no longer credible because any rapid progress will be attributed to the drugs
Test boosters (e.g. boron) sold by influencers like More Plates More Dates are garbage that makes teens hyper-focus on T levels instead of training
Training is what boosts natural testosterone, not supplements or TRT
Give lifestyle fixes 6 months, or 1-2 years if your lifestyle was terrible, before considering anything else; viewers who did this reported normal bloodwork
